public_body: Woburn Public Library Board Of Trustees
overall: Board violated the OML by inadequate remote meeting capacity, non-roll-call votes, late minute approvals, and two unposted deliberations (intentional, no penalty); other allegations rejected. Ordered compliance, training, and minutes approval.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board's September 10 remote meeting lacked adequate public access because no telephone option was offered alongside Zoom.
allegations.key_passage: As the Board is not required to provide more than one means of adequate, alternative access, we find that the Board did not violate the Law where it chose to allow public access to its September 10 meeting only through the web-based Zoom platform, without also providing access by telephone.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the September 10 remote meeting's Zoom capacity of 100 participants was insufficient, so interested members of the public could not join.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board’s September 10 meeting was not accessible to the public, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board did not take all votes by roll call during its September 10 remote meeting, including officer elections and adjournment.
allegations.key_passage: As the Board did not take all votes during the September 10 meeting by roll call, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law as alleged.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged that non-Board microphones were muted and the Zoom chat disabled during the September 10 meeting, preventing public participation.
allegations.key_passage: As the Open Meeting Law leaves public participation to the discretion of the public body’s chair, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law where the Board did not allow members of the public to speak or communicate using the chat function during a September 10 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not read her emailed written communication at the November 12 meeting, though the notice listed a 'communications' topic.
allegations.key_passage: we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law where the Board chose not to read such communications, because whether to accept public comment during a public body’s meeting, and the manner in which to do so, is within the discretion of the chair.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board failed to approve minutes in a timely manner for meetings from the first half of 2020 and a December 2019 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: For these reasons, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve meeting minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged a quorum of the Board deliberated at an unposted October 2, 2020 special meeting to authorize a public relations payment.
allegations.key_passage: Since no meeting notice was posted for this meeting, we find that the Board deliberated outside of a posted meeting, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged a quorum of the Board approved hiring outside counsel at an unposted October 5, 2020 meeting in the Library Director's office.
allegations.key_passage: As no notice was posted for the October 5, 2020, meeting, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a posted meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged five Board members deliberated during an August 26, 2020 archives visit at the Library, which was not posted as a meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that the Board deliberated during this on-site inspection, and therefore the Board was not required to post notice of the on-site inspection and did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this respect.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged Board members used the August 26 archives visit to discuss, serially, replacing the Board president, leading to a September 10 vote.
allegations.key_passage: However, as we find no specific evidence of serial deliberation, we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law related to the August 26 archives visit.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Board emails about scheduling and distributing documents before meetings amounted to deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Board emails we reviewed which merely relate to scheduling meetings are not deliberations under the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a quorum of the Board coordinated nearly identical letters to the editor and an MLN response letter outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: For this reason, we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law regarding the four Board members’ letters to the editor.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may result in a civil penalty.
All current Board members must attend an Open Meeting Law webinar training presented by the AG's office within 90 days of receipt and certify completion within 95 days.
Approve minutes of the December 3, 2019, October 2, 2020, and October 5, 2020 meetings within 30 days of receipt, to the extent possible from available records, and make them public.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may result in the imposition of a civil penalty.

source.publisher_filename: DETERMINATION - 7 7 2021 - OML 2021-91 - WOBURN PUBLIC LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES.pdf

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
